summary: Several large functions in the SSE/request-building hot loop bypass care; one wasted re-clone on the Incompatible-strict path; one identity-allocation helper that looks like a round-trip sanitize; one parallel convert_messages across the two protocols that duplicates user/tool-result extraction.

findings.title: parse_sse_event_multi is a single 300+ line match across 16+ variants
findings.description: The `parse_sse_event_multi` function contains the entire StreamEvent variant dispatch as a single `match` with inline extraction logic per arm (item_to_call HashMap mutation, OutputItem reconstruction, usage extraction, error mapping, reasoning delta emission). This is the largest function in the file (lines 470-790) and dwarfs the rest of the parser's complexity. Both `ensure_openai_tool_envelope` and `normalize_node` in openai_strict_schema.rs already carry `rust-doctor-disable-next-line high-cyclomatic-complexity`; this function has no such waiver and is significantly more complex than either.
findings.fix_proposal: Extract per-variant handlers (e.g. `parse_text_delta`, `parse_function_call_args_delta`, `parse_completed`, `parse_failed`) into private free functions, each taking a `&mut StreamParseState` (item_to_call + pending). Then `parse_sse_event_multi` becomes a 16-arm match that just routes the parsed event to the right one.

findings.title: build_tools wastes `td.parameters.clone()` on Incompatible-strict path
findings.description: The strict-normalization branch clones `td.parameters` twice on the `StrictResult::Incompatible` arm: the first clone is mutated by `normalize_strict_schema`, then the assignment `params = td.parameters.clone()` discards it to start fresh for `lenient_multi_type_rewrite`. The first clone is only necessary for the `Ok` arm; on `Incompatible` it could be skipped, or the second clone avoided by running `lenient_multi_type_rewrite` over the partially-normalized `params` (it is idempotent and tolerates prior transforms). This wastes one deep `serde_json::Value` clone per Incompatible tool per request — the path that fires precisely when a tool schema is already complex.
findings.fix_proposal: Restructure as: `let mut params = td.parameters.clone();` once at the top, then either `normalize_strict_schema(&mut params, true) → Ok` (keep) or on `Incompatible` simply run `lenient_multi_type_rewrite(&mut params)` in place. The lenient pass is a no-op on already-normalized subtrees and handles fresh ones.

findings.title: convert_messages walks UnifiedMessage in both Chat and Responses adapters
findings.description: Both `openai_chat/proto_impl.rs::convert_messages` (lines 67-170) and `responses/shared.rs::convert_messages` reimplement the same three-arm walk over `UnifiedMessage` (User/Assistant/ToolResult). The user-text extraction, the Assistant tool-call serialization, and the ToolResult text join are byte-equivalent shape decisions; only the wire-shape output diverges (Message vs InputItem). ~100 lines of `filter_map(...).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n")` plumbing appears in both.
findings.fix_proposal: Extract a small helper module (e.g. `providers::protocols::unified_extract`) exposing `extract_user_text(content) -> String`, `extract_assistant_text(content) -> String`, `extract_assistant_tool_calls(content) -> Vec<ToolCallTuple>`, `extract_tool_result_text(content) -> String`. Each adapter then walks UnifiedMessage once and dispatches the tuples into its wire shape.

findings.title: build_request is 250 lines of inline JSON construction
findings.description: The single `build_request` function (lines 53-280) builds the wire body by ~15 inline `body["..."] = json!(...)` writes gated by capability/option checks. Each capability branch (prompt_cache, response_format, seed, logprobs, top_logprobs, tools, tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, service_tier, stop, reasoning_effort, max_tokens, frequency/presence penalty, top_p, temperature) is 5-20 lines. The function dwarfs the rest of the file and carries the `rust-doctor-disable-next-line high-cyclomatic-complexity` waiver — exactly the signal that it has crossed the threshold where extraction pays.
findings.fix_proposal: Extract per-section builders (`apply_max_tokens`, `apply_sampling`, `apply_reasoning`, `apply_stop`, `apply_prompt_cache`, `apply_response_format`, `apply_tools`, `apply_tool_choice`, `apply_capability_gated_extras`) each taking `&mut serde_json::Value` and `&ProviderConfig`. `build_request` becomes a thin orchestrator.

findings.title: parse_chat_sse_event is a single 200-line function with five inline sub-parsers
findings.description: The function (lines 22-220) handles in-band error mapping, usage extraction (with two payload-shape fallbacks for cache_read_tokens), tool-call delta buffering, finish_reason → StopReason translation, and tool-call-end emission inline as one `serde_json::Value` match body. Each concern is independently testable but currently entangled.
findings.fix_proposal: Extract `parse_usage(&Value) -> Option<TokenUsage>`, `parse_choice_delta(&Value, &mut IndexIdTracker, &mut VecDeque)`, `parse_finish_reason(&str) -> Option<StopReason>`, then `parse_chat_sse_event` becomes a 30-line orchestrator that calls each.

findings.title: stream_deltas inline SSE state machine mixes parser, deferral, and truncation guards
findings.description: The `unfold` body in `stream_deltas` (lines 300-450) carries the State struct with seven fields (`bytes`, `line_buf`, `index_tracker`, `pending`, `deferred_done`, `done_emitted`, `done`) and a single `loop` that interleaves line parsing, deferral calls (`defer_done_until_usage`), buffer-bounds checks, and end-of-stream truncation guards. The truncation-guard logic at the bottom (release deferred Done, decide whether to emit Timeout) is conceptually a separate concern that is currently tangled with byte-reading.
findings.fix_proposal: Extract `try_parse_line(line: &str, state: &mut State) -> LineAction` returning whether to continue/drain/terminate, and `finalize_truncation(state: &mut State)` handling the end-of-stream guard. The unfold body then becomes a tighter three-arm dispatch.

findings.title: OpenAiToolCall.call_type carries #[allow(dead_code)] — unused field
findings.description: The `OpenAiToolCall` struct (inbound) has `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the `call_type` field. The outbound type is `OpenAiToolCallOut` (which sets `call_type: "function"` unconditionally). The inbound field is set in `proto_impl.rs::convert_messages` (line ~155) but never read on the outbound conversion path. The annotation suggests this field was kept for symmetry with the wire shape but the inbound deserializer does not actually need it.
findings.fix_proposal: Remove `call_type` from `OpenAiToolCall` entirely, or remove `#[allow(dead_code)]` if downstream readers do consume it. Verify with `rg "call_type"` against `src/providers/openai/types.rs` callers.

findings.title: desanitize_tool_name is an identity function that allocates unconditionally
findings.description: `desanitize_tool_name(name: &str) -> String` does no transformation — the comment claims it reverses `sanitize_tool_name`'s underscore substitution but the implementation simply calls `.to_string()` and returns. Every caller that holds an owned `String` could instead hold the `&str` it already had, and every caller that needs an owned `String` could call `.to_string()` themselves. The "desanitize" naming implies a transformation that does not happen, which is worse than a missing function.
findings.fix_proposal: Either (a) remove `desanitize_tool_name` and have callers use the input `&str` or call `.to_string()` directly, or (b) implement the actual reversal (replace `_` with original character, requiring a mapping table), or (c) rename to `to_owned_tool_name` and drop the misleading "desanitize" framing.

findings.title: is_local_host allocates a HashSet on every call
findings.description: `is_local_host(host: &str) -> bool` constructs `HashSet::from([...])` containing four loopback entries on every invocation. The function is called from `detect_endpoint_class`, which itself runs per request-build. A 4-entry `&[&str]` linear scan is faster than the hashmap build for this size and removes the per-call allocation.

findings.title: extract_tool_calls silently swallows JSON parse errors by falling back to String
findings.description: `extract_tool_calls` deserializes each tool call's arguments string into a `serde_json::Value`; on failure the function logs nothing, drops the error, and stores the raw string in the output. A malformed argument stream that reaches the consumer is indistinguishable from a perfectly-valid one — which is precisely when downstream validation would benefit from knowing.
findings.fix_proposal: On parse failure, return `Result<...>` with the original string preserved AND the underlying `serde_json::Error`, or at minimum emit a `tracing::warn!` with the call id and error. The function is the one place the wire-time deserialize error can be reported before downstream code treats the call as well-formed.

findings.title: lenient_rewrite_node lacks the high-cyclomatic-complexity waiver used by sibling parsers
findings.description: In the same file, both `ensure_openai_tool_envelope` (line 60) and `normalize_node` (line 297) carry `// rust-doctor-disable-next-line high-cyclomatic-complexity` comments. The sibling `lenient_rewrite_node` (lines ~167-220) has the same nested-match + recursive shape but no such waiver. With clippy running at `-D warnings` per AGENTS.md, this is a build flag inconsistency that risks regressing on the next strict-mode lint bump.
findings.fix_proposal: Add `// rust-doctor-disable-next-line high-cyclomatic-complexity` immediately above `pub fn lenient_multi_type_rewrite` (and consider the inner `lenient_rewrite_node` too) to match the sibling waiver pattern.

findings.title: MessageContent is `untagged`, mixing Text and Multimodal discrimination
findings.description: `MessageContent` uses `#[serde(untagged)]` to discriminate between `Text(String)` and `Multimodal { content: Vec<ContentBlock> }`. An untagged enum on a public wire type silently accepts whichever shape the JSON matches first — for a value like `null` or `[]` the choice is order-dependent. The Responses-side equivalent uses a typed enum; this one does not.
findings.fix_proposal: Switch to `#[serde(untagged)]` only after verifying both variants are reachable from `UnifiedMessage::User` — or change to `#[serde(tag = "type", content = "content")]` so the wire format is self-describing. Trade-off: changes the wire shape for any persisted/recorded message.

findings.title: validate_provider_base_url errors are logged, not propagated
findings.description: `build_endpoint` calls `validate_provider_base_url` in both the Codex and standard branches and only emits `tracing::error!`. The sibling `openai_chat/adapter.rs::build_endpoint` does the same; the comment in chat says "Match the sibling adapter behaviour... The earlier return of the *unvalidated* raw_base_url let a tampered preset smuggle non-HTTP schemes into the URL parser for this protocol alone." This means the fix for the chat adapter (return an error) was not propagated here — both protocols share the same bug.
findings.fix_proposal: Match the chat-adapter behavior of returning an error or apply the agreed-upon policy of logging-and-falling-through consistently across both adapters. If the policy is intentional, document it in one place (the http_client module) and reference it from both call sites.
